title: By the sky and the one that comes by night.
subtitle: An oath by a visitor in the dark
then: The surah came when the Makkans were using every plan to defeat the Quran's message. Qatadah said the star is called Tariq because {idea}it is only seen at night and hidden during the day{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ named this surah as a fitting recitation for Maghrib.
now: You drive home late and one bright star sits over the motorway. {idea}It was there all day, you just could not see it.{/idea} Some truths only show up when it gets dark.
old: If I cannot see something, it is probably not there.
new: Some things are always there and only show themselves at night.
try: Step outside after dark tonight and find one star.

title: And what will make you know what the night comer is?
subtitle: A question to make you look up
then: Ibn Kathir notes that Allah asks the question, then explains it in the next verse. {idea}The Quran often slows the listener down before a sign{/idea}, so it is not passed over.
now: You have seen the night sky so often you no longer look. {idea}The question is a tap on the shoulder: look again, properly.{/idea}
old: I already know what is up there.
new: What I have stopped noticing may still have something to teach me.
try: Look properly at one ordinary thing today that you usually ignore.

title: It is the star that pierces the dark.
subtitle: Light that cuts through
then: Ibn Abbas said Ath-Thaqib means {idea}the illuminating{/idea}. Ikrimah said it illuminates and {trap}burns the Shaytan{/trap}. A small point of light, sworn by.
now: One honest friend in a toxic workplace. One prayer in a messy day. {reward}A small light still pierces a big dark.{/reward}
old: One small good thing cannot change a dark situation.
new: A single point of light is enough to pierce the darkness.
try: Be the one small light somewhere today: a kind word in a tense room.

title: Every soul has a guardian over it.
subtitle: What the oath was for

row.title: no one is looking out for me

then: Ibn Kathir says every soul has {reward}a guardian from Allah that protects it from calamities{/reward}, citing the angels in succession before and behind a person. The introduction adds that nothing in the universe survives without a guardian.
now: The near miss on the road. The fall you walked away from. The illness caught early. {reward}You were guarded more times than you know.{/reward}
old: I am basically on my own out there.
new: Allah has set a guardian over me, every moment.
try: Recall one near miss in your life and thank Allah for the guard you did not see.

title: So let man look at what he was made from.
subtitle: A humble origin, a strong argument
then: Ibn Kathir says this alerts man to {trap}the weakness of his origin{/trap}, and its aim is to guide him to accept the Hereafter, {idea}because whoever can begin creation can repeat it{/idea}.
now: You hold an ultrasound print of a baby the size of a bean. {idea}Every argument you have ever won started there.{/idea}
old: I am self-made, and I find resurrection hard to believe.
new: I came from almost nothing, so returning me is easy for my Maker.
try: Look at a baby photo of yourself today and remember where you started.

title: He was made from a gushing fluid.
subtitle: The humble start of every human
then: Ibn Kathir says the child is produced from the fluid of both man and woman {idea}by the permission of Allah{/idea}. The verse states it plainly to show how simple the start of a person is.
now: The CEO, the influencer, the professor, and the newborn in the incubator. {idea}Same beginning.{/idea} Any pride you carry started as a drop.
old: Some people are simply made of better stuff.
new: Every one of us began the same humble way, by Allah's permission.
try: Treat one person you usually look down on with full respect today.

title: Coming from between the backbone and the ribs.
subtitle: Both parents, one child
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman{/idea}, and that the child is not born except from both of them.
now: Your mother's patience and your father's laugh show up in you. {reward}You came from both of them, by Allah's design.{/reward} Gratitude to them is part of seeing the sign.
old: How I was made is just biology, nothing more.
new: My coming from my two parents is a sign of Allah's careful making.
try: Make dua for both your parents today, by name.

title: He is surely able to bring him back.
subtitle: The conclusion of the argument
then: Ibn Kathir says He is able to repeat his creation and resurrect him, which {idea}is clearly possible, because whoever can begin creation can surely repeat it{/idea}. The introduction says this is the surah's first theme.
now: A builder who put up a house from bare ground can certainly rebuild it. {idea}You already accept that logic everywhere else.{/idea}
old: Being raised after death sounds hard to believe.
new: The One who made me from a drop can easily bring me back.
try: When you wake up tomorrow, say the morning dua and think of it as a small rising.

title: The Day when secrets are tested.
subtitle: Nothing stays hidden
then: Ibn Kathir says on that Day {trap}the secret will be made open and the concealed will be well known{/trap}. He cites the hadith that every betrayer will have a flag raised for him naming his betrayal.
now: The deleted messages, the second account, the promise you broke quietly. {idea}Secrets can also be good: the charity no one saw, the night prayer.{/idea} Both come out.
old: What I keep private will stay private forever.
new: Every secret, good or bad, will be brought out on that Day.
try: Add one good secret to your record today: a hidden charity or a quiet prayer.

title: Then he has no strength and no helper.
subtitle: Alone with what you did
then: Ibn Kathir says man will have no power within himself and no helper from outside. {trap}He will not be able to save himself, nor will anyone else save him.{/trap}
now: Here you can call a friend, hire a lawyer, borrow from family. {idea}That Day the phone list is empty.{/idea} {reward}What you send ahead now is your help then.{/reward}
old: There will always be someone who can bail me out.
new: On that Day only my deeds and Allah's mercy will help me.
try: Send one good deed ahead today as if it were your only helper.

title: By the sky that returns the rain.
subtitle: A second oath, about provision
then: Ibn Abbas said it means rain that falls and then falls again. Qatadah said {reward}it returns the sustenance of the creatures every year; without it they and their cattle would perish{/reward}.
now: You turn the tap and water comes. Bread is on the supermarket shelf. {reward}Every bit of it traces back to rain that keeps returning.{/reward}
old: Rain is just weather, nothing to think about.
new: Every rainfall is Allah returning my provision to me.
try: Next time it rains, say the dua for rain or simply thank Allah for it.

title: And by the earth that cracks open with growth.
subtitle: Life breaking through the ground
then: Ibn Abbas, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Ikrimah and others said it means {reward}splitting to bring forth plant growth{/reward}. The introduction says rain and growth are no child's play, but serious work.
now: A green shoot forcing its way through a crack in the pavement outside your flat. {idea}Small, stubborn, unstoppable.{/idea}
old: Plants growing is just nature doing its thing.
new: Every sprout breaking the soil is a sign of how the dead will rise.
try: Notice one plant growing somewhere unexpected today and say subhanAllah.

title: This Quran is a decisive word.
subtitle: What the second oath confirms

row.title: the Quran
sub: sworn to by sky and earth

then: Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said fasl here means {idea}true{/idea}; someone else said {idea}a just ruling{/idea}. The surah introduction calls it a decisive Word that no plan of the disbelievers can defeat.
now: Two loud opinions in the family chat, five videos saying opposite things. {idea}You need a word that settles it.{/idea}
old: Everything is opinion, so nothing really settles a question.
new: The Quran is the word that separates truth from falsehood for me.
try: Bring one question you are confused about to the Quran today and look up a related verse.

title: And it is no joke.
subtitle: Serious words deserve serious attention
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}rather it is serious and true{/idea}. The introduction links it to the rain and plants: just as these are no child's play, the Quran's truths are no jest.
now: Memes quoting verses, jokes about the Day of Judgement, a verse used as a punchline. {trap}It is easy to slide into treating it lightly.{/trap}
old: A little joking about religion is harmless.
new: The Quran is serious, so I handle its words with care.
try: Next time a verse comes up in a joke today, gently change the subject.

title: They are plotting a plot.
subtitle: Scheming against the message
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}plot against the people, calling them to oppose the Quran{/trap}. The introduction says the Makkans were using every device to defeat the message.
now: You are not plotting against the Quran. {idea}But you may be quietly plotting around it: the excuse ready for skipping prayer, the clever reason a verse does not apply to you.{/idea}
old: I am not scheming against anything.
new: I should check whether I am scheming around what Allah asks of me.
try: Notice one excuse you use to avoid a good deed. Drop it today.

title: And I am planning a plan.
subtitle: Allah's plan over every scheme
then: The introduction says the deniers thought their plans would defeat the Quran, but {idea}Allah too is devising a plan which will bring all their scheming to nothing{/idea}.
now: Someone at work is plotting to push you out. A relative is turning family against you. {reward}You do not have to out-scheme them. There is a better Planner.{/reward}
old: I have to out-plan everyone who works against me.
new: Allah's plan stands over every scheme, including the ones against me.
try: Hand one situation where you feel schemed against to Allah in dua today.

title: So give the deniers time. Leave them a little while.
subtitle: Patience, not panic
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {idea}wait for them and do not be in haste concerning them{/idea}, for a little while. The introduction calls it consolation for the Prophet ﷺ and a quiet warning to the deniers.
now: You want to reply to the nasty comment right now, fix the injustice tonight, prove them wrong this week. {reward}Some things are better left to Allah's timing.{/reward}
old: If I do not react right away, wrong will win.
new: I can wait patiently, because Allah's timing is better than mine.
try: Hold off one angry reply today. Wait a day before deciding.
